doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

chapter: Sound Pieces and Los Angeles studios
title: Name that tune and the Sound Pieces recording
summary: A quiz from The Kennedy Dream, Hentoff's liner notes, and the difficulty of the music for the original players and the Smithsonian.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Thank you for saying that. I wanted to read a couple more quotes. First of all, name this tune. You ready?
You’ll have to forgive my vocalizing.
I love it. And Nat Hentoff, who wrote more than one set of liner notes for your father over the years, he was talking about “Sound Pieces” and he said, “There are no arcane
implications to this music,” followed by your father saying, “It could be for trombone and snare drum.” So my question is, and it’s sort of a broad question—
And I answered that wrong by the way but that’s okay.
Yes. You knew it was “Sound Pieces,” yes.
As a matter of fact I have —
Actually it was written for French horn if you listen to it, and he had French horns playing really high on that thing. The Smithsonian did it and some of those guys were scuffling.

You know I’m sort of glad — not glad — I find that interesting also, the fact that you said in the original session that cats couldn’t cut it. Because we tend to think that at that level they’re infallible. They can just play — people like to say first time perfect. Right? Not necessarily so.
No. And if the music is tough you’ve got to woodshed that stuff just like anybody else does.
